instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Challenge by Proxy
cards.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've held up my red card after yours. You tell the director we reject the new overtime rule; I'll back you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red means I'm here for the afternoon session. I wasn't voting against anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, afternoon business. You bring up the overtime rule in that session; I'll support the complaint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you put your name on the complaint with mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave a second line for me. Once he's agreed to hear you out, I'll come up and sign it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed out my court booking like you did. Tell the captain we're protesting his queue-jumping rule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cancelled because my ankle hurts. I still want a court next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, we're protecting next week's bookings. You ask him to end queue-jumping before you rebook.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll cancel that booking too if I complain. Come with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You ask first. If he offers you next week's court, wave me over and I'll tell him I support you.

cards.title: Use the Proper Title
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on my paper hat for the introductions, like you. Announce 'Director Patel is ready' before the staff barbecue starts, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hats keep hair out of the food. Everybody serving wears one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Then announce 'Director Patel will be serving burgers.' They should know who's doing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just writing our names on the hats so people know who to ask for things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'Director Patel' on mine, then. Large enough for the back of the burger queue.

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked my workshop plan like you ticked Morgan's. Which of us are you backing at the meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My tick means I've checked the costs. I like your location and Morgan's budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, cost checks. When you recommend that combination, whose proposal will you call it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A compromise. I'll put both your names on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put one name first. Which of us will you put above the other?

beats.text: I've pinned a ribbon to my bag like you. Will you wear mine or Nina's when we elect the chess-club chair?

cards.title: Obey Without Explanation
cards.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tapped your desk twice, so I've tapped mine. Bring that empty box over here, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking whether the desk wobbles. What do you need the box for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, checking. Put it on my desk first; I'd like one request carried out before the questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on your desk. Can I get back to packing now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it back and bring it here once more. This time, stay until I tell you to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pulled the curtain up like you. Leave your desk and stand by the window until I say you can move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only wanted more light on the accounts. Why do I have to stand there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, better visibility. Stand where I can see you following the instruction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The window's open. I'm freezing; can I fetch my coat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fetch mine as well, then come back to the window and hold it for me.

cards.title: Pass Me the Authority
cards.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've held up my keys like you. Tell the committee I'm the one who decides now, before you retire.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was looking for my car key. You can have the hall key; let me get my coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, sorting the keys. Before the coat, tell them to bring their decisions to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking me now whether Saturday's dance is cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them 'Ask Jo; Jo decides.' Then ask me about the dance while they're listening.

beats.text: I've turned my chair towards yours. Are you handing over the meeting? Tell everyone I'll decide the next item.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned away from the glare. I do have to leave, but there's still the budget vote.

beats.speaker: A
